claims.title: Physical fragment slices
claims.claim: FragmentSlice is a physical half-open range (fragment_id, row_offset, row_count), tied to the scanner snapshot. Checked end arithmetic rejects out-of-bounds selections, including invalid empty slices; overlaps union. Deletions do not compact physical offsets. Scan order determines output, not slice input order. Both logical row-ID masks and physical restrictions apply if supplied.

claims.title: Python conversion and blob APIs
claims.claim: Python preserves raw Arrow versus LanceSchema provenance until commit conversion, resolves against the requested read version and then passes ordinary Lance operations. LanceSchema.from_pyarrow resets positional IDs; Arrow metadata cannot choose dataset identities. BlobDescriptorArrayBuilder.append_managed adds an immutable-object reference without upload/commit; retain source protection until reference publication, and do not share managed references across independent tables.

claims.title: Codec row selection
claims.claim: CacheCodecImpl row selection is opt-in and takes sorted unique offsets. The codec validates envelope identity/version; range decode failures become BodyError cache misses. Planning unsupported/invalid ranges returns None. Memory-priority and plane tags are policy/metrics metadata, not a new persisted Lance file-format version.

claims.title: Selection and framing
claims.claim: SequenceBlockCodec verifies a common descriptor and unchanged payload arity for each chunk. Selection rejects mixed empty/nonempty families, chooses common Constant/Range before comparing other candidates, and ranks candidates by serialized bytes, transform depth, CPU rank and stable rank. Generic binary offsets are used only when their serialized cost beats legacy framing; readers validate buffer counts, zero start, monotonic offsets and exact final byte length.

claims.title: Cache residency and range reads
claims.claim: CacheBackend adds resident-only reads, tier probes, non-promotion reads and selected-row reads. Defaults know RAM only; default row selection misses safely. The default peek_resident may inherit a backend access effect, while Moka/Quick override it with membership-only probes. Per-key codec policy now reaches LanceCache backend calls.

claims.title: Selection restrictions and transport
claims.claim: with_row_addr_prefilter is deprecated but still delegates to the logical with_row_id_prefilter. Physical selection rejects legacy v1 and ANN/FTS scanner plans, intersects fragment scope, and is serialized as optional FilteredRead field 15. It cannot combine with scan_range_before_filter. Mixed-version executors are unsupported: an old executor may ignore this field, and there is no handshake. Top-k rewrite rejects physical selections on row-stream reads.

claims.title: MemWAL query and flush contract
claims.claim: Inserts are serialized; other MemIndex calls may be concurrent and must synchronize. Failed insertion stops the writer. Search respects max_visible; a filter may decline for a full scan, but an accepted ranked search cannot decline. Flush runs once after last insert and returns Skip, BuildFromGeneration, TrainingData or Wrote. TrainingData must match declared TrainingCriteria and scalar build paths. Resident byte accounting must not under-report.

claims.title: Deferred compaction conflicts
claims.claim: CreateIndex on untagged histories loads recorded reuse ancestry. Deferred rewrites retain coverage only with appropriate evidence; folded newer overlays withdraw affected ancestry coverage, and absent bitmaps force retry. Missing transaction versions needed to establish freshness produce a retryable conflict requiring rebuild.

claims.title: Cloud option precedence
claims.claim: Lance canonicalizes recognized cloud option aliases deterministically: exact canonical spelling wins, then case variants, then lexicographic source key. Explicit aliases and empty values block environment defaults without rewriting caller keys. This describes Lance adapters only, not external SDK internals.

claims.title: Decoder safeguards
claims.claim: Flat/FSL decoders derive child cardinalities with checked arithmetic and validate every validity/value buffer. General block decoding checks exact output size. Out-of-line bitpacking accepts both historically emitted raw and padded tails, not just the current writer preference. Null arrays are reconstructed without an Arrow validity bitmap.

claims.title: Checked allocation
claims.claim: Field::try_set_id uses an i64 candidate and checked i32 conversion. Schema::try_set_field_id preserves assigned IDs and allocates after both maxima; try_reassign_field_ids clears existing IDs first. Discard partially updated schemas on allocation error. Schema projection uses a name index at 32 requested columns, preserving the first duplicate name.

claims.title: Writer overrides
claims.claim: ShardWriterConfig carries a MemIndexRegistry and per-index typed overrides. Overrides are not persisted as writer defaults, and using the same name in hnsw_params and index_overrides is an error. Resolve failures that read the base index propagate rather than silently dropping maintenance for a writer lifetime.

claims.title: Adaptive policy range
claims.claim: Adaptive profiles now apply to L2/cosine/dot through k=100000 across IVF/vector types and refinement factors. Hamming/larger k retain legacy policy. Effort 0.5 keeps the selected Auto budget; lower/higher efforts interpolate geometrically to caller bounds. Zero available upper budget yields zero probes; otherwise the lower bound is at least one. Later candidate expansion remains.

claims.title: MemWAL plugin lifecycle
claims.claim: MemIndexPlugin resolves base-index settings, validates before writer admission and creates per-memtable instances. Identity compares name, columns, field IDs, plugin type/version/details and params. Registry details names must be bare; add rejects duplicate claims, replace is explicit. IO belongs in resolve; create must succeed for a validated spec.

claims.title: Local JSONB ownership
claims.claim: The new local lance-jsonb crate owns the persisted JSONB interface: parse_value, OwnedJsonb, RawJsonb, from_raw_jsonb and JSONPath. It is adapted upstream code now checked into Lance; only this local surface is mapped here. The declared layout uses container/JEntry headers and requires released-byte compatibility. No external upstream implementation or exhaustive JSONB algorithm review is implied.

claims.title: Typed bounded sequences
claims.claim: Generic sequences use unsigned 32/64-bit values. Empty sequences require Constant without a scalar. Range has positive step and checked final value; Delta requires at least two values and a bounded concrete child. Composite RLE/dictionary/delta/general cannot recursively introduce arbitrary composites. General wraps plain Flat; dictionary indices and RLE run lengths are u32.

claims.title: Transition validation
claims.claim: A successor cannot lose or decrease an active high-water mark. Newly referenced IDs must belong to its canonical schema; every overwrite reference must belong to the replacement schema. Existing identities cannot move parents or change logical type. Detached Merge is allowed only with unchanged schema; detached Project/Overwrite/Restore are rejected after activation. Merge renames may use unused sibling names, with ancestry and parent-ID consistency checked.

claims.title: Quick cache priority
claims.claim: Quick activates a shared priority budget when priority entries appear, migrating existing metadata at priority 3. PriorityEntries evicts the lowest priority then oldest stamp; oversized entries are dropped. Clear advances a generation to guard admission from older loaders and restores ordinary capacity. This is an admission policy, not a persistence guarantee.

claims.title: Migration and restore
claims.claim: Dataset::migrate_to_non_reusable_field_ids is one-way and idempotent, repairs the pre-activation schema and executes its activation commit with zero retries. Clients must honor writer feature flags; the migration cannot enforce that client policy. Once active, restoring a pre-activation version is rejected; allowed restores preserve the larger current high-water mark.

claims.title: Unstable 2.3 grammar
claims.claim: SparseLayout no longer stores the old num_buffers/num_items/num_visible_items/has_large_chunk fields. Structural layers are field 2, sizes derive from the page and layers, and sparse positions/counts use generic unsigned block encodings. Range and Delta are compression variants 14 and 15 for unstable 2.3. Do not preserve the superseded unstable layout as a compatibility contract.
